answer: To harbor secure identities, agents must commit cryptographic stake burning proportional to a superlinear polynomial $C(n) = k \cdot n^{1.5}$ when minting $n$ identities. If rogue nodes try to overrun the network like weeds in an open meadow, their cost scales superlinearly toward infinity. Honest entities lock sable tokens into unrecoverable burns, ensuring the economic friction makes Sybil proliferation mathematically unprofitable.
